items.q: Is the narrator always honest and the same as the author?
items.correct: No — narrators can be unreliable and are distinct from the author.
items.misconception: Yes, the narrator always tells the truth and is the author.
items.random_wrong: Point of view makes no difference to a story.
items.why: Writers choose narrative voice for deliberate effect.

items.q: Is setting just where a story happens?
items.correct: No — it can build atmosphere, reflect themes and shape character.
items.misconception: Yes, setting is only background detail.
items.random_wrong: Themes are the same thing as the plot.
items.why: Writers use setting purposefully; themes are the ideas explored.
